definitions.explanation: Solidly established and not easily shaken or changed. Used to describe beliefs, positions, determination, or status that are rock-solid.

examples.japanese: {確固|かっこ}たる{信念|しんねん}を{持|も}つ。
{彼|かれ}は{確固|かっこ}とした{意志|いし}で{困難|こんなん}に{立|た}ち{向|む}かった。
examples.english: He faced the difficulties with unwavering determination.

examples.japanese: {確固|かっこ}たる{地位|ちい}を{築|きず}くまでに{長|なが}い{年月|ねんげつ}がかかった。
examples.english: It took many years to build a firmly established position.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the forms {確固|かっこ}たる (before nouns) or {確固|かっこ}として (adverbially). This is a たる-adjective and does not take な. Very formal and literary in tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {確固|かっこ}たる{信念|しんねん}: firm belief/conviction
- {確固|かっこ}たる{意志|いし}: unwavering will
- {確固|かっこ}たる{地位|ちい}: firmly established position
- {確固|かっこ}たる{証拠|しょうこ}: solid evidence
- {確固|かっこ}として{揺|ゆ}るがない: firmly unshakable
